reviewed.disposition: Explicit bootstrap/cutover marker is file-owned under original plan section 3. Pending creation is exclusive, synced and maintenance-owned; activation requires matching operation, inventory and schema bindings under the same owner.

Requires writer exclusion, maintenance ownership and verified archival. It publishes immutable attachment objects and a SQLite backup, verifies logical parity and integrity before marker activation, then records the publication journal. Journal writes are maintenance checkpoints, not task mirrors.

Maintains explicit publication-stage journals and independently retained backup bundles. Staging obtains maintenance ownership and verifies candidate/bundle bindings; recovery refuses rebuilding after marker or database publication and retains interrupted attempts.

Under maintenance ownership and explicit writer exclusion, records archival progress and moves inventoried legacy roots to retained archive. It revalidates source partition and excludes immutable attachment roots from archival; no normal-path task file writer.

Explicit interchange export runs from a consistent storage snapshot and uses assertPortableExportDestination before task output allocation. Named writes produce portable artifact/event/session/catalog files and attachment outputs; export is not a live mirror.

Writes independent backup manifests and attachment inventories in exclusively allocated directories. Uses a committed SQLite backup, verifies referenced attachment bytes and digest bindings; restore backup output is fresh and independently verified.

Maintains owner-checked restore preparation journals and independently retained rebuild intents. Interrupted snapshots are retained before rebuilding from a fingerprint-bound, verified backup; temporary intent publication uses exclusive link semantics.

Writes an explicit target-version validation receipt only after source-pinned legacy checkout validation, exact task catalog parity, every-task protocol validation and final retained-byte verification. Maintenance is released only after validation; not normal-path operational writing.

Writes a replacement ownership journal after retained outgoing evidence and exact maintenance-owner continuity checks. It does not mutate the independently retained outgoing manifest or operational task rows.

limitations: This source-role audit classifies named static atomic writes only. Transitive aliases and other publication primitives remain outside this inventory.
Maintenance checkpoints are explicitly supported bootstrap/migration file roles under the original plan; classification alone is not proof of every recovery path or current platform acceptance.
